## Paper

Artificial Intelligence, Algorithm Design, and Pricing

## World

pricing_arena

## Institution

Pricing algorithm design / learning-protocol variation.

## Agent type

Q-learning and neural pricing algorithms.

## Theoretical benchmark

Learning-protocol changes can shift pricing outcomes between competitive and supra-competitive regimes.

## Learning setup

Capability ladder over tabular Q, DQN, PPO, independent-DQN, and centralized critic under matched pricing institutions.

## Metrics

Collusion indices, exploitability, price/profit/welfare, price dispersion, and mind-by-institution effects.

## Main result

Synchronous updating leads to competitive pricing outcomes aligning with Nash equilibria, while asynchronous algorithms with limited economic sophistication generate supra-competitive prices that converge more slowly.

## What they prove

Learning protocol design influences pricing outcomes; synchronous updating leads to Nash equilibrium convergence; asynchronous algorithms with economic reasoning reduce supra-competitive pricing

## What they only simulate

Convergence behavior of pricing algorithms in repeated Bertrand games; impact of initial conditions on price outcomes

## What they do NOT test

Long-term market dynamics beyond the simulated pricing game; real-world market interactions and regulatory constraints

## What we need to reproduce

Interpret capability differences as algorithm-design effects and show matched comparisons across minds and institutions.

## How our project differs

The paper studies algorithm-design choices in pricing. This repo generalizes that discipline into a cross-world capability ladder.

## Implementation obligations

Same institution set across minds; full n=20 outputs; fixed independent-DQN replacement; synthesis table separating capability effects from mechanism effects.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

outputs/phase3_full/mind_comparison.csv; build_world_mind_comparison.py; build_cross_world_synthesis.py.

## Failure modes to audit

Attributing differences to economics when training protocol changed; keeping alias mind rows; failing to report uncertainty/paired effects.

## Project code comparison

Compare Artificial Intelligence, Algorithm Design, and Pricing to the Phase 3 ladder outputs. The repo's contribution is not just another pricing run; it tests whether algorithm capability changes institution robustness.
